title: Travel Allowance on Single Specialist Referrals — Primary Care Provider Assignment
content:
**Training note, Primary Care Provider Assignment: the travel allowance on a single specialist referral.**

**Q. When are travel visits added to a single specialist referral?**
For members who travel far for care. They are added to the referral's visits before the single-referral visit ceiling is applied.

**Q. What is measured?**
The longest one-way distance of the member's completed medical-appointment transportation legs on record under **Non-Emergency Medical Transportation**: legs recorded as completed, with the trip purpose medical appointment, compared by their one-way miles. Every such leg on record is measured, whatever its date.

**Q. How many visits?**

| Longest completed medical-appointment leg (one-way miles) | Travel visits added |
|---|---|
| 30.0 or more (the far distance) | 2 (the two-visit travel allowance) |
| At least 15.0 but less than 30.0 (the middle distance) | 1 (the one-visit travel allowance) |
| Less than 15.0, or no such leg | 0 |

**Q. What happens right at the band edges (hypothetical legs)?**
A longest leg of exactly 30.0 miles adds 2; 29.9 miles adds 1; exactly 15.0 miles adds 1; 14.9 miles adds nothing.

**Q. Does a long trip for another purpose count?**
No. A completed 35.0-mile leg whose purpose is dialysis or a pharmacy visit is not a medical-appointment leg. With medical-appointment legs of at most 16.2 miles, 1 travel visit is added.
